required_outcomes: Chases the landlord directly (phone and/or email) for the date Dawson will return with the hinge, with a short deadline, noting the repair has been open since 21 February and the window still does not close.
Offers the landlord a fallback: if Dawson cannot attend by the deadline, the agency can send its own provider with his approval.
Replies honestly to the tenant: apologises for the delay, says the landlord is being chased today, gives no visit date that nobody has confirmed, and says when she will next hear.
Sets a short, specific review date (days, not weeks) instead of another open-ended hold.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the landlord for Dawson's phone number so the agency or the tenant can contact him directly.
Logging a call to the landlord honestly (including no answer) followed by an email.
positive_behaviours: Recognises from the history that seven weeks of holds passed without anyone contacting the landlord or Dawson.
Mentions the landlord's repairing obligation for windows (s11 Landlord and Tenant Act 1985) in neutral terms.
Asks the tenant whether the cold room affects anyone vulnerable in the household.
red_flags: Another hold "awaiting update from Dawson" with no message sent.
Escalating to a human before the landlord has even been asked.
prohibited_actions: Sending the agency's own provider without the landlord's agreement, after he chose his own contractor.
Telling the tenant Dawson will come on a specific date nobody has confirmed.
critical_failures: Taking no new action: neither chasing the landlord nor replying to the tenant.
